title: Getting your workers doing what you want
target: How to direct a worker in TCG Card Shop Simulator without standing over them: the interaction screen the tasks hang off, the two price options on the price screen, the paged list of pack types and the two separate permissions a cashier counter has.
version: no version stated by this build (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shop that is open and running
At least one worker you can interact with
Some idea of which job you want the worker to take on

steps.do: Start from the worker rather than from a settings menu.
steps.because: the task screen hangs off the worker's own interaction screen rather than sitting in a general options list (WorkerInteractUIScreen, WorkerSetPrimarySecondaryTaskScreen)

steps.do: Set both the main task and the second task before you walk away.
steps.because: the screen is for a primary and a secondary task, so leaving one unset leaves the worker with nothing to fall back on (WorkerSetPrimarySecondaryTaskScreen)

steps.do: Deal with the price options on the price screen, not by trusting the worker.
steps.because: the price screen carries separate selections for rounding a price up and for whether the worker may set card prices at all (m_RoundUpPriceTickImage, m_CanSetCardPricePriceTickImage)

steps.do: Read the multiplier as a direction, not only a number.
steps.because: the screen shows a multiplier as a percentage and gives it a positive or a negative colour, so the worker's rule can push a price either way (m_MultiplierPercentText, m_PositiveColor, m_NegativeColor)

steps.do: Page through the pack list instead of assuming the first screen is all of it.
steps.because: the pack-type screen shows a list of panels with next and previous buttons, so the choices do not all fit on one page (m_WorkerPackTypeOptionPanelUIList, m_NextPageBtn, m_PreviousPageBtn)

steps.do: Check whether a pack type is locked before you rely on it.
steps.because: each pack-type panel has a locked group of its own alongside its name, image and tick (WorkerPackTypeOptionPanelUI, m_LockedGrp, m_TickImage, m_NameText)

steps.do: Treat checkout and trading at a counter as two permissions.
steps.because: the counter setting screen keeps a tick for checkout and a separate tick for trading, so granting one does not grant the other (SetCashierCounterSettingScreen, m_CanCheckoutTick, m_CanTradeTick)

steps.do: Set each worker up on their own rather than once for the whole staff.
steps.because: the screens are per worker and the game ships worker icons for each of them, so two workers can be given different jobs (Icon_Worker0, Icon_Worker1)

commonMistakes: Setting a main task and leaving the second task empty.
Letting a worker set card prices when the price rule they work to has not been set.
Assuming a pack type is available when its panel is still locked.
Expecting trade permission at a counter to follow from checkout permission.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
